episodes.181200: During the evening of July 24th, a decaying thunderstorm produced a microburst wind gust that caused damage to a residential solar array just southwest of Moriarty.
episodes.181201: In the midst of hot and muggy conditions ruling the roost over the Central Appalachians, diurnally driven showers and thunderstorms thrived near the end of July. On the afternoon of July 24th, a few storms that originated in southeast Ohio crossed over the river into West Virginia. One particular storm that passed over Wood County resulted in strong damaging winds that day and caused downed trees in and around the Parkersburg area. Locally heavy downpours also resulted in a small creek to rise out of its banks briefly in the town of Mineral Wells.
episodes.181203: A few thunderstorms sprouted on July 24th in southeast Ohio during an unseasonably hot end to the month. These pop up storms produced downburst winds as they dissipated, which resulted in instances of downed trees and power lines in Perry and Meigs Counties.
episodes.181409: Widespread showers and thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain in central New Jersey on the afternoon of July 25.  Rainfall amounts were as high as 1.5 to 2.5 inches.
episodes.181412: Widespread showers and thunderstorms produced locally heavy rain in southeastern Pennsylvania on the afternoon of July 25.  Rainfall amounts were as high as 2.0 to 3.5 inches.
episodes.181507: A weak cold front passed through, but with plenty of moisture and weaker flow aloft, some slow moving storms produced instances of flooding and flash flooding around Baltimore County.
episodes.181592: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed over central Pennsylvania during the early afternoon hours, with a couple of cells producing wind damage. Storms eventually coalesced into a broken line of discrete cells that crossed the Susquehanna Valley during the evening hours, producing sporadic wind damage.
episodes.181611: Building instability and a weak mid-level disturbance helped trigger scattered thunderstorms late in the afternoon into very early evening. The strongest storms occurred across the Rochester Metro as repeated storms formed along a lake breeze boundary. Reports of sporadic wind damage were received across the city of Rochester.
episodes.181633: A weak disturbance moved through Central New York and kicked off isolated thunderstorms. Due to clearing of skies and daytime heating, the environment became unstable enough to support one severe thunderstorm in Sullivan County.
episodes.181690: Strong to severe thunderstorms associated with shortwave troughs erupted over eastern New York during the afternoon hours on July 24th and July 25th resulting in multiple reports of downed trees and wires.
episodes.181892: A couple of thunderstorms produced localized wind damage over the eastern West Virginia panhandle.
episodes.181894: Remnant outflow from convection the day before over the Midwest combined with a lee pressure trough resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. Several produced localized wind damage and some hail.
episodes.181895: Remnant outflow from convection the day before over the Midwest combined with a lee pressure trough resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. Several produced localized wind damage and some hail.
episodes.181943: Remnant outflow from convection the day before over the Midwest combined with a lee pressure trough resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. Several produced localized gale- to storm-force winds over area waterways.
episodes.182039: A trough pushes through the Nature Coast and West Central Florida following the longwave pattern. This helped to enhance the already moisture and unstable southwest to westerly flow. This resulted in numerous strong marine wind gusts once again.

episodes.182255: A thunderstorms with heavy rainfall stalled over the communities of Peru, Jay, and Canton on the evening of the 25th. Radar estimates between 3 to 4.5 inches fell between 6 and 730 pm. The rain fell over saturated ground and hilly terrain. A small tributary called the Tucker Valley Brook came out of banks and washed out a bridge on the Jay-Wilton line.
episodes.182256: Showers and thunderstorms developed along a slow moving sea breeze boundary across central Androscoggin County on the afternoon into early evening of the 25th. The storm produced rainfall rates between 2 and 3 inches an hour on top of already saturated soils. This ended up leading to multiple instances of flash flooding, specifically in the Cities of Auburn and Lewiston.  In addition to the more significant flash flooding, trees were reported down in numerous locations due to convective outflow winds.

episodes.182648: A few isolated storms developed in the afternoon and evening within a very moisture and unstable atmosphere. One storm became severe and produced localized wind damage.
episodes.182703: A seasonably strong shortwave trough brought scattered severe storms to Massachusetts during the afternoon and evening. Persistent and redeveloping storms also lead to flooding issues.

episodes.183363: A cluster of thunderstorms formed over Ohio during the late afternoon and early evening hours of July 24th, as weak disturbances aloft sparked convection in an unstable atmosphere. The slow-moving storms impacted Coshocton County most keenly with wind damage and flash flooding.

As those storms settled southeast into the foothills of eastern Kentucky during the mid and late evening, they encountered a more stable environment and weakened. However, a one robust storm cell was still strong enough to produce two instances of wind damage in Bath County.
episodes.183783: Severe thunderstorms produced very strong wind gusts over parts of Adams, Denver and Weld counties.  Peak gusts ranged from 60 to 70 mph.

episodes.183899: Monsoonal thunderstorms occurred on July 25 in the Riverside County Mountains and San Diego County Mountains. Locally heavy rainfall of 0.50-0.75 was reported in Riverside County, and a lightning strike ignited a small wildfire in San Diego County.
episodes.183945: There were two areas of severe thunderstorms this day. Around Rock Springs, high based thunderstorms moved into an area with an almost 60 degree dew point depression. A maximum wind gust of 62 mph occurred at the Sweetwater County airport. A line of thunderstorms associated with a shortwave also moved into Teton County. A 61 mph wind gust was reported at the Jackson Hole airport. In Wilson, many trees were downed, resulting in the loss of power for several hours.
episodes.183960: Numerous gale-force wind gusts occurred in association with a cluster of thunderstorms that moved southwest off the south Florida mainland.  A deep Saharan Air Layer was exiting the Florida Keys coastal waters to the west.
episodes.183985: Isolated thunderstorms developed over the North Carolina mountains and foothills during the afternoon. One of the storms produced brief large hail over McDowell County.

episodes.184091: A strong mid-level shortwave trough moved into a very moist and unstable environment, with scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developing. Thunderstorms produced damaging winds and large hail across parts of eastern Pennsylvania.

episodes.184124: Multiple severe thunderstorms developed along a surface trough west of the area and then moved east through southeast NY. Outflow from these storms continued to spark severe thunderstorms as it moved east. The severe storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184134: Multiple severe thunderstorms developed along a surface trough west of the area and then moved east through northeast NJ. Outflow from these storms continued to spark severe thunderstorms as it moved east. The severe storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184136: Multiple severe thunderstorms developed along a surface trough west of the area and then moved east over the waters. Outflow from these storms continued to spark severe thunderstorms as it moved east. The severe storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184240: A strong area of high pressure brought very warm temperatures to much of the Interior on July 24th. A weak disturbance moved along the south side of the area of high pressure resulting in scattered thunderstorms forming over the Interior. Some of these storms brought strong winds and large hail.
episodes.184255: A large ridge of high pressure was centered over the Great Lakes and Ohio Valley on July 25th, 2023. Convection developed along a lake breeze from Elyria, OH northeast to Erie, PA, just south of the I-90 corridor, as surface based CAPE values built to 2000-3000 j/kg by early afternoon. Little to no deep layer bulk shear promoted a pulse thunderstorm environment, with isolated thunderstorms building and collapsing within a 30-60 minute period. A few of the storms produced large hail and damaging winds from microbursts. One slow moving, back-building storm produced isolated flash flooding in the Chagrin Falls area.
episodes.184278: High wind gusts occurred with damage reported.
episodes.184419: While the synoptic scale pattern on July 24th and 25th, 2023 had a similar appearance to earlier events in the month with large scale troughing across the Ohio Valley, the flow aloft was generally weaker, which limited the overall severe potential to more of a typical summertime event. On the other hand, instability values were quite impressive, with 2500-3500 J/kg of mixed-layer CAPE developing across central Kentucky and southern Indiana during the afternoon hours on July 24th. Convection initiated in the vicinity of a weak surface frontal boundary across southwestern Indiana and southern Illinois during the early afternoon hours, with storms moving off to the east and southeast along with the background flow aloft. The parameter space was generally favorable for ordinary cell thunderstorms, with a few multicell clusters also developing along and ahead of the front. The primary observed severe hazard was damaging straight-line winds, as between 1000-1400 J/kg of downdraft CAPE was observed on mesoanalysis data. Additionally, a couple instances of severe hail were also observed in southern Indiana, where significant hail parameter values were slightly higher (around or above 1). Storms gradually subsided after sunset on July 24th, with conditions remaining quiet through the morning and early afternoon hours on July 25th. While slightly drier air moved into southern Indiana and north central Kentucky and limited thunderstorm potential on July 25th, a few strong to severe storms developed across southern and southwestern Kentucky during the afternoon and evening hours. One of these storms was strong enough to produce severe hail near Burkesville in Cumberland County, Kentucky.
episodes.185767: A mid/upper-level trough lingered over the Great Lakes and Middle to Upper OH Valley during the afternoon of the 23rd through early evening of the 25th as embedded shortwave disturbances traversed northern OH generally from west to east. Multiple surface trough axes associated with the disturbances moved generally eastward across northern OH. Low-level convergence and associated ascent along surface trough axes acted as a focus for scattered thunderstorm development during the early evening of the 23rd. These multicell thunderstorms generated isolated straight-line convective wind damage as they persisted northeastward and encountered moderate MUCAPE and marginally-moderate effective bulk shear. Low-level convergence and associated ascent along a Lake Erie lake breeze front generated scattered thunderstorms in the Cleveland metro area during the afternoon of the 25th. The pulse thunderstorms produced isolated severe hail and straight-line convective wind damage as they persisted generally southward and encountered strong MUCAPE and weak to marginally-moderate effective bulk shear.

As the event unfolded the flooding extended to southern Lewiston over Adams Avenue near the Public Works Department, and flooded parking lots at Bates College.
